seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Spring, TX 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Spring, TX: Old Town Spring, City Place tree lighting, Meyer Park, a tree farm train ride and a drive-thru light show.
lede: Spring celebrates Christmas in Old Town Spring's historic village, on the plaza at City Place and in Harris County Precinct 3 parks, with a drive-thru light show and a train ride at a tree farm.
celebrates: Old Town Spring is the heart of the season. Its Improvement District promotes the holidays as Hometown Holidays, opening with a Grand Christmas Tree Lighting at the Spring Historical Museum on Main Street, with Christmas movie nights at the museum and holiday sponsors that include Union Pacific. City Place on Lake Plaza Drive holds its own tree lighting by the lake and free holiday story times and kids shows on its plaza. Harris County Precinct 3 hosts Christmas in the Park at Meyer Park, and families can drive through The Light Park's light show off Interstate 45.
lastyear: Old Town Spring's holiday season has gone by the name Home For The Holidays, which is still the title of its Facebook page for the village at Preston Avenue. For the 2026 season the Old Town Spring Visitors Bureau promotes it as Hometown Holidays and describes the Grand Christmas Tree Lighting as a holiday tradition that has lasted for generations. The village is known for historic shops, restaurants and hide-aways on its old streets, and the season keeps that small-town setting.
facts: Spring began as a farming community. The Texas State Historical Association says William Pierpont opened a trading post on nearby Spring Creek in 1838, and German immigrants, including Carl Wunsche, began farming the land in the mid-1840s. The town had a sugar mill and two cotton gins. Old Town Spring became a shopping village after the Old Town Spring Association formed in 1980, and by 1989 it had more than eighty specialty shops. From 1969 to 1992 the Goodyear airship America was based near Spring.
trains: Spring grew up on the rails. After the Houston and Great Northern Railroad built through town in 1871, Spring grew considerably, and in 1901 to 1903 the International-Great Northern Railroad connected it with Fort Worth. A roundhouse followed, and Spring became a major switchyard with fourteen trackyards and about 200 rail workers, until the roundhouse moved to Houston in 1923. Today Union Pacific is listed among Old Town Spring's holiday sponsors, and a tree farm in Spring runs Christmas train rides. For a longer train day, try the railroad museums in Rosenberg and Galveston.

The Spring Historical Museum shows holiday films on Saturday evenings during the season.
City Place lights its holiday tree by the lake and adds a gingerbread village, a holiday market and live music.

kidfact: Spring was once a railroad town with a roundhouse and fourteen trackyards, and a blimp named America was based nearby for more than 20 years.
faq: What is Hometown Holidays in Old Town Spring?

Hometown Holidays is the name the Old Town Spring Visitors Bureau uses for the village's Christmas season. It opens with the Grand Christmas Tree Lighting at the Spring Historical Museum on Main Street and includes Christmas movie nights at the museum.
Are there free Christmas events in Spring?

Yes. The City Place tree lighting, City Place story times, Christmas in the Park at Meyer Park, the Barbara Bush Branch Library open house and the Spring Historical Museum movie nights are listed as free on the host pages linked from this page.
Can kids ride a train in Spring at Christmas?

Yes. Old Time Christmas Tree Farm runs Christmas train rides and Santa visits on its season weekends. Train rides and other attractions use attraction tickets sold at the farm, while farm entry is free.
Is there a Christmas light show in Spring?
The Light Park runs a drive-thru Christmas light show in the Hurricane Harbor Splashtown parking lot off Interstate 45. Tickets are sold per car, and the show runs rain or shine.
Why is Spring known for trains?

The Houston and Great Northern Railroad built through Spring in 1871, and a roundhouse and major switchyard followed in the early 1900s. The Texas State Historical Association describes Spring as a railroad town until the roundhouse moved in 1923.

intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in Spring for 2026, and here is what he found: 8 family events, 6 of them free. The magic runs from November 6 (The Light Park Spring Drive-Thru Christmas Lights) through January 3, 2027 (the same light show), with November 27 (Christmas Train Rides and Santa at Old Time Christmas Tree Farm), November 29 (Oh, What Fun Holiday Tree Lighting Celebration at City Place) and December 5 (Christmas in the Park at Meyer Park) along the way. We check every date on the host's own website, and each listing links straight there.
